title_en: Commentary on al-Mughnī al-Mufīd — Tape Thirteen
body_ar: "باب من جحد شيئا من الأسماء والصفات" عقد هذا الباب لنوع آخر مما يضاد التوحيد ويخالفه وهو نفي التوحيد في الأسماء والصفات، بمعنى أن يجحد الإنسان بعض الأسماء أو بعض الصفات فينكرها، أو يجحدها جميعا، فالذي ينكر كل ذلك فقد جحد الجميع جحد أسماء الله وصفاته، والذي ينكر الصفات دون الأسماء كذلك، والذي ينكر بعض الصفات دون بعض كذلك،
body_en: 'Chapter: on one who denies something of the names and the attributes.' This chapter was set down for another category of what runs counter to the oneness of God (tawḥīd) and conflicts with it, namely the negation of God's oneness in His names and attributes — in the sense that a person denies some of the names or some of the attributes and rejects them, or denies them all. The one who rejects all of that has denied the whole: he has denied God's names and His attributes. The one who rejects the attributes but not the names is likewise, and the one who rejects some of the attributes but not others is likewise,

flags.context: The title of the series, appearing in the title of articles 502–516.
options: al-Mughnī al-Mufīd (left untranslated as a work title)
The Sheikh's commentary series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd
flags.note: Article 516 shows the series expounds Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, and article 508 quotes the base text in verse, so al-Mughnī al-Mufīd appears to be a versification (naẓm) of that book rather than a separate work by the Sheikh. The Sheikh's office should confirm the work and its author before the title is translated or expanded anywhere in the corpus; it has been left untranslated for now.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

This page belongs to the Sheikh's tape series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, identified in article 516, the first tape of the series. Passages in quotation marks are the base text being commented on; the unquoted text is the Sheikh's own commentary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved.

The excerpt states the chapter's subject but breaks off before any ruling is given on the three cases the Sheikh distinguishes. The repeated كذلك ('is likewise') has no completed predicate in the written source; the English leaves it equally open rather than supplying one.
